simple.meaning: נָכֵא (nâkêʼ) is a Hebrew word meaning “smitten , i.e. (figuratively) afflicted.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: נָכֵא (H5218) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Proverbs 15:13, with occurrences in Proverbs, Isaiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נָכֵא (H5218) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in נָכֵא (H5218) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: נָכֵא (nâkêʼ) / H5218 is traced through Proverbs 15:13, Proverbs 17:22, Proverbs 18:14, Isaiah 16:7 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H5218. nake ' [ נָכָא ] adjective stricken ; — masculine plural נְכָאִים Isa 16:7 (Kö ii. 1, 73 ), of Moab prostrated by conquest. [ נָכֵא ] adjective id., always feminine נְכֵאָה רוּחַ a stricken spirit , Prov 15:13 ; 17:22 (both opposed to שָׁמֵךְַ לֵב ), 18:14 .
